A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SAE Match, with the same central method and substantial overlapping experiments. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and rendered figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gemma 2 experiments on feature matching, semantic similarity, feature persistence, layer pruning and SAE sparsity.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds reconstruction comparisons, sparsity and quantile analyses, and Llama-3.1-8B results and feature-path examples.

M1.justification: The core folded-parameter matching and permutation composition remain unchanged. Appendix B adds a quantile-dependent pruning variant: low-MSE features use the target-layer decoder, while remaining features use the source-layer decoder (Equation 6), modifying reconstruction without replacing SAE Match.

E1.justification: The documented corpora remain OpenWebText, Code and WikiText, and the tasks remain feature alignment, persistence and hidden-state approximation. The Llama extension adds model/SAE configurations; no additional data domain or distinct task is identified.

E2.justification: Figure 7 adds unfolded matching to the Matching Score comparison. New Figure 11 compares layerwise pruning against unfolded matching and current/previous hidden-state reconstruction. Some controls already appeared in v1's sparsity experiment, but their participation in these comparisons is new.

E3.justification: v3 adds Llama-3.1-8B evaluation, an experiment selecting SAEs with similar l0 values across layers, and quantile-based evaluation protocols. Table 1 also changes checkpoint l0 identifiers at layers 0, 1 and 25 from 46, 40 and 55 to 102, 108 and 116, respectively. These are reported setting revisions; they do not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New analyses test whether adjacent-layer sparsity differences explain early-layer failures (Figure 15), how MSE-based feature selection affects reconstruction (Figures 16–17), and where matching underperforms simple reconstruction (Figure 11). The original encoder/decoder ablation and sparsity sweep remain, renumbered as Figures 12 and 14.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, seed-based uncertainty, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. Existing MSE distribution plots remain unchanged; the new MSE quantiles control feature selection rather than estimate uncertainty.

E6.justification: v3 adds results for Llama, reconstruction controls, comparable-sparsity SAEs and quantile selection, including evidence of matching errors in early layers. Figure 10 also contains revised loss and explained-variance trajectories. Given the revised checkpoint listings, these curves do not establish controlled, same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Equation 4 corrects bias folding from decoder bias to encoder bias. Appendix B introduces the quantile partition and hybrid reconstruction definition in Equation 6, while Section 2 generalizes the background sparsity penalty to L_reg. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contributions retain the same claims about data-free alignment, folding and feature persistence. The conclusion newly claims applicability beyond Gemma 2, citing the added Llama results.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 replaces the early-layer polysemanticity/description explanation with an account centered on differing SAE l0 values, supported by Figure 15. Sections 5.5–6 add matching-error and bijective-matching limitations. The earlier description-error caveat is removed, although Figure 7's caption still retains the old polysemanticity explanation.

D1.justification: Table 1 revises checkpoint identifiers and adds a direct Gemma Scope resource link. Figure 8 explicitly describes score averaging, and Figure 19 identifies LlamaScope residual 32K SAEs in its image labels. The existing evaluation prompt and main sampling details are retained.

R1.justification: The discussion and bibliography remove Gurnee et al. (2023), previously used to support the early-layer polysemanticity explanation. The remaining citations and positioning relative to SAEs and permutation-based weight matching are substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and most main-text prose remain substantially unchanged. Local revisions clarify hypotheses and rewrite the early-layer discussion and conclusion; a new quantile appendix shifts the later appendix labels. Author affiliations and the publication header are also updated.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands the visual evidence with reconstruction-control, Llama, sparsity-selection and quantile plots, plus Llama path examples. Figure 7 gains a comparison curve and legend, and Figure 10 is replotted. Original Figures 11–13 survive as Figures 12, 14 and 18; the Gemma path images are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added reconstruction controls and sparsity/quantile tests better support the paper's account of when matching fails, while Llama results provide evidence beyond Gemma. These gains are tempered by limited documentation of the Llama evaluation protocol, removal of the description-error caveat, and Figure 7's retention of an explanation superseded in Section 5.3. Overall, the empirical diagnosis improves more clearly than the paper's completeness and consistency.
